title: mini-ops-sync-console-telemetry-checkin-2026-12-15
body:
Mini Ops sync — Console & Tooling: telemetry-focused check-in
Date: 2026-12-15 09:30 PT (15m)
Attendees: Maya T (notes), Ravi P, Luc M, Elaine C, (brief ping from SRE: Jonas)

Purpose: quick telemetry pulse on current panel rollout (panel-v2) + a short UI regressions watchlist. Keep it tight — action-oriented.

High-level updates
- Rollout status: panel-v2 at 18% canary across hosted (us-west1). Canary policy: 5/party -> 25% over 48h if steady.
- Observed: panel render error rate baseline +12% over last 3h (primarily Firefox 119 on macOS). Slow frames and occasional blank card renders.
- Analytics pipeline: ingestion lag spiked to ~45m for events from the canary cohort between 02:30–03:15 UTC. Backfill running but delays cause stale dashboards.

What we checked quickly
- Client console errors: Frequent stack traces pointing to async layout hydration race in panel.js: hydratePanel -> computeLayout when server TTL is omitted. (See linear INF-2345).
- Feature flag distribution: rollout client cohort size confirmed. No unexpected routing by region.
- SRE: no infra-related OOMs or autoscaler events tied to the spike. GPU/worker metrics look steady.
- Analytics: Kafka partition skew noticed for the partition receiving canary events; backlog cleared after reassign but introduced lag.

Decisions made during sync
- Pause progressive increase to 18% (freeze at 18%) until short mitigation deployed. Hold remaining increases. (Owner: Maya)
- Quick client-side patch: guard in hydratePanel to bail if layout inputs missing; release as hotfix PR and promote to canary. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/789 (Ravi to shepherd).
- Telemetry dashboard: add a short-lived filter for browser.ua to isolate Firefox 119 macOS and add alert for blank-card rate >1%. (Owner: Luc)
- Analytics infra: SRE to check partitioning strategy and add temporary consumer parallelism to catch up faster; follow-up with infra postmortem if backlog returns. (Owner: Jonas)

Notes / Observations (unpolished)
- Repro: Elisa in CS reproduced blank card locally with network RTT >200ms + content-length 0 response simulated. Sounds like hydration ordering + missing fallback render.
- There are two related Linear tickets: INF-2345 (client hydration race) and INF-2351 (dashboard alert for blank-card). Cross-link them.
- Risk: if we continue to increase canary %, we risk surface-level UX regressions that seed user support noise. Recommend keeping error budget tight.

Action items (short list)
- Maya: freeze rollout progression and communicate to PM + support (today EOD).
- Ravi: land and merge hotfix PR; coordinate canary deploy to 18% within 2 hours of merge. (ETA: 2026-12-15 12:00 PT)
- Luc: add ad-hoc telemetry filter and alert, update dashboard legend. (ETA: 2026-12-15 14:00 PT)
- Elaine: draft short FAQ for CS with repro steps + temporary mitigation notes. (ETA: 2026-12-15 17:00 PT)
- Jonas (SRE): investigate Kafka partition skew root cause and increase consumer parallelism for backfill; update infra incident ticket. (ETA: 2026-12-16)

Follow-ups / questions
- If hotfix doesn't reduce blank-card rate by >=70% in 2h, we revert canary to previous build and open rollback playbook. Who triggers rollback? (Tentative: Maya + Jonas)
- Need a retro on why a client-only hydration race created server-visible telemetry noise; backlog for engineering: add deterministic unit test covering hydration ordering. (Owner: eng-qa)

Random notes to self (scratch)
- Might be worth exploring small synthetic canary run against Firefox farm (BrowserStack) before increasing percent next time.
- Could we add KV-cached fallback HTML to avoid blank-card visible to users until hydration completes? Low effort but could mask deeper issue.

Meeting ended: 09:48 PT — short sync.

Links / refs:
- Linear INF-2345, INF-2351
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/789
- Confluence: confluence.internal.redwood.com/console/rollouts/canary-plan-2026-12

Status: draft notes — will publish minutes to Confluence after hotfix merge and telemetry check.
